title: Elasticsearch Search & Analytics
description: Query Elasticsearch indices with search, ES|QL, mappings, and shard inspection via the official Elasticsearch MCP server.

env_vars.name: ES_URL
env_vars.description: URL of the Elasticsearch cluster (e.g. https://your-cluster.es.cloud:9200). Required to connect; use https:// for TLS in transit.

env_vars.name: ES_API_KEY
env_vars.description: Elasticsearch API key (preferred). Use a key scoped to read-only access on the target indices; pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: ES_USERNAME
env_vars.description: Username for basic authentication (alternative to ES_API_KEY).

env_vars.name: ES_PASSWORD
env_vars.description: Password for basic authentication; pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: ES_SSL_SKIP_VERIFY
env_vars.description: Set to `true` to skip SSL/TLS certificate verification. Development/testing only — never use against production clusters.

auth.recipe: set ES_URL to your cluster URL and authenticate with an API key (ES_API_KEY, preferred) or basic auth (ES_USERNAME + ES_PASSWORD); scope the key read-only to the target indices.

sample_tools.name: get_mappings
sample_tools.summary: Get field mappings for a specific index.

sample_tools.name: search
sample_tools.summary: Run an Elasticsearch search using Query DSL.

sample_tools.name: get_shards
sample_tools.summary: Get shard information for all or specific indices.

known_limitations: Requires an Elasticsearch cluster URL (ES_URL) plus credentials — an API key (ES_API_KEY) or basic auth (ES_USERNAME/ES_PASSWORD); without them the server cannot reach the cluster.
Distributed as a Docker image (docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch) — Docker must be installed and running; the legacy npm package is deprecated at 0.3.1.
Read-only over your cluster — list/search/mappings/shards/ES|QL only; no document- or index-mutation tools are exposed.
The standalone server is in maintenance mode (critical security fixes only); Elastic's successor is the Agent Builder MCP endpoint in Elasticsearch 9.2.0+.
Destructive-action audit (X2.18): no destructive tools — the server exposes read-only query tools only.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `elastic`: { command: docker, args: [run, -i, --rm, -e, ES_URL, -e, ES_API_KEY, docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch, stdio], env: { ES_URL: "https://...", ES_API_KEY: "..." } }.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `elastic`, command `docker run -i --rm -e ES_URL -e ES_API_KEY docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch stdio`; set ES_URL + ES_API_KEY in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `elastic` (VS Code Insider, MCP preview); supply ES_URL + ES_API_KEY via inputs.
